hypothesis: Six-permutation position balancing cancels linear drift but may retain apparent treatment bias under one-slot carryover.

run_conditions.local_test_result: 7/7 passed twice in fresh Linux directories with compatible local simulator shim; exact committed v1 upstream tested by hosted CI.
run_conditions.hosted_result: 93/93 tests on Ubuntu and 93/93 on Windows; both jobs reproduced canonical LF JSON SHA-256 a17e1ded6268fe8497347a6d14086e45230e2cfc7eee5fe8498dadd4c6064e31
run_conditions.newline_failure_learning: Earlier run #40639428614 passed working-tree byte equality but produced different raw Windows stdout SHA-256 4a667f95a1f889ada60a672f48e42f3536dcc3ee888b35066c5d2b306287858b due to CRLF translation. Fixed source stdout LF and pinned canonical digest; do not reinterpret earlier raw hash as cross-OS reproducibility.

results.negative_result: Position balancing does not guarantee elimination of one-slot carryover bias.

limitations: No physical measurements or instrument authentication.
Assumed additive one-slot carryover is not calibrated to a device.
The frequency of biased permutations is not a probability of real-world outcomes.
No causal prototype performance or energy claims.
A genuine logging dry run and controlled physical comparison remain TBD.
